props.gloss_en: one rescues the casing of a [Torah] scroll together with the scroll
...even though there are coins inside them
a fourteenth that falls on Shabbat: one flays the Paschal lamb up to the breast
the Sages: one flays all of it
granted for R' Yishmael: its need-on-High has [already] been done
R' Yochanan: the verse says 'all that the Lord made is for His sake' (Prov 16:4) [-- the Sages' reason]
Rav Yosef: [His sake here is] that it not putrefy
Rava: that sacred things of Heaven not lie like a carcass
the difference between them: where it is laid on a golden table
...or a day of a cold north wind
and R' Yishmael uses 'the Lord made for His sake' [to teach] that one not remove the sacrificial parts before flaying the hide
why? Rav Huna son of Rav Natan: because of the hairs
reading 1: the colleagues said: if one rescues the scroll's casing with the scroll, shall we not flay the Paschal lamb of its hide?
Rav Ashi: they dispute over two things -- they dispute over moving
...and they dispute over the labour
reading 2 (Rav Ashi): they said: if one rescues the scroll's casing with the scroll, shall we not move the hide along with the flesh?
reading 3: if one rescues the scroll's casing with the scroll even with coins inside, shall we not move the hide along with the flesh?
reading 4: if one brings a casing with coins inside from elsewhere to rescue a Torah scroll in it, shall we not move the hide along with the flesh?
[the premise of reading 4:] one may bring a casing with coins inside from elsewhere to rescue a Torah scroll in it
Mar bar Rav Ashi: and as for your difficulty, here moving and here labour -- [it speaks of] where he has no need of the hide
Abaye and Rava: R' Shimon concedes in [a case of] 'cut off its head and will it not die?' -- [one is liable]
where he takes it [the hide] off in strips
